note: A new player's first changes with a backing track: Em and Am, two bars each, over drums and bass with the keys left out so the guitar plays the chords. The why says what a backing track teaches (keep the hand moving, let the chord catch up), the step names what Play starts and where to look, and the one extra line is what to do when a change comes late. The tempo is moves; the key stays, since the open shapes are the lesson.

exercise.title: Em and Am with a backing track
exercise.why: A backing track keeps going whether your change is ready or not, so playing with one teaches you to keep the strumming hand moving and let the chord catch up.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the backing track: drums and bass, two bars of Em and then two bars of Am. The lit chord box shows the chord to play, and you strum down once on every beat.
If a change comes late, keep your strumming hand going and join in on the next beat 1.
